answer: Seats are drawn, never claimed. Each epoch the beacon is hashed with an operator key to pick who grades, and the same hash derives an avoidance set, so two keys of one owner cannot share a panel. Clones buy nothing: each extra identity locks a stake before the lottery admits it, and the draw spreads them across peers. Siblings that meet lose both stakes. Shifting one vote means funding redundant stakes, so cost rises where farming pays. The beacon is no more steerable than water crossing karst, none can forge it, and each honest signature is a signal of a seat earned, not bought.
